rules.text: The Armor table lists the game’s main armor. The table includes the cost and weight of armor, as well as the following details:

rules.title: Category
rules.text: Every type of armor falls into a category: Light, Medium, or Heavy. The category determines how long it takes to don or doff the armor (as shown in the table).

rules.title: Armor Class (AC)
rules.text: The table’s Armor Class column tells you what your base AC is when you wear a type of armor. For example, if you wear Leather Armor, your base AC is 11 plus your Dexterity modifier, whereas your AC is 16 in Chain Mail.

rules.title: Strength
rules.text: If the table shows a Strength score in the Strength column for an armor type, that armor reduces the wearer’s speed by 10 feet unless the wearer has a Strength score equal to or higher than the listed score.

rules.title: Stealth
rules.text: If the table shows “Disadvantage” in the Stealth column for an armor type, the wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

rules.title: Armor Training
rules.text: Anyone can don armor or hold a Shield, but only those with training can use them effectively, as explained below. A character’s class and other features determine the character’s armor training. A monster has training with any armor in its stat block.

rules.title: Light, Medium, or Heavy Armor
rules.text: If you wear Light, Medium, or Heavy armor and lack training with it, you have Disadvantage on any D20 Test that involves Strength or Dexterity, and you can’t cast spells.

rules.title: Shield
rules.text: You gain the Armor Class benefit of a Shield only if you have training with it.

rules.title: One at a Time
rules.text: A creature can wear only one suit of armor at a time and wield only one Shield at a time.

groups.name: Medium Armor
groups.note: 5 Minutes to Don and 1 Minute to Doff

groups.name: Heavy Armor
groups.note: 10 Minutes to Don and 5 Minutes to Doff

groups.name: Shield
groups.note: Utilize Action to Don or Doff
